items.html: Mongolian licence plates are mostly white with a hint of red on the left side from the Soyombo symbol.

Mongolia primarily uses Cyrillic script, though Latin and traditional Mongolian script can also occasionally be seen. Mongolian Cyrillic contains the letters Ɵ and Ү, which do not exist in the Russian alphabet. Additionally, the use of double vowels, such as aa, ƟƟ or ЭЭ, is common in Mongolian.

NOTE: The letters Ɵ and Ү also exist in the Kyrgyz and Kazakh languages.

Mongolia very often has a visible Street View car as all of Mongolian coverage was driven with a large pickup truck. The truck can have several features such as a tent on top, red side-view mirrors, a snorkel, and roof-racks. All of these can be of help in identifying Mongolia.

Mongolia can typically be identified by the steppe biomes found across the country. While some forested areas are found in Mongolia, most of the country features empty grasslands or deserts with a characteristic lack of trees. It is not uncommon to find rugged, rocky or rolling hills as well as rivers and lakes across Mongolia.
Mongolia uniquely features white bowling-pin shaped bollards with two red stripes around the top.

Mongolian infrastructure has clear Russian influence. Wooden poles with supporting stone blocks, white lamp posts, and three-striped pedestrian crossing signs are common to see.

Unique to Mongolia is the “ЗОГС” stop sign.

NOTE: Each town has unique lamp post designs, so learning them can be quite useful.
Mongolian neighbourhoods are very frequently separated by dirt alleys and wooden fences.
White, round yurts are the traditional dwelling of nomadic families in Mongolia, and are often seen all around the country.
It is very common to see large herds of animals in Mongolia, including horses, yaks, cows, sheep, goats, and camels.
Decorated piles of stones, known as ovoos, are used as ceremonial markers or shrines throughout Mongolia and are common to see.

Mongolia has very limited coverage, mainly along highways and in large towns. Learning which roads and towns have coverage can be very useful. The highest coverage density can be found around the capital of Ulaanbaatar.

NOTE: Mongolia has lots of hidden coverage that will generally not be discussed in the guide.

_You can click on the map to enlarge it._

Driving directions can be a very useful clue for narrowing down your location in Mongolia. In general, the driving direction tends to be away from Ulaanbaatar.

_You can click on the map to enlarge it._

Mongolia has a very flat landscape in the east and in the south, with rolling hills in the north, and large mountains and rocky hills being common in the west.

_You can click on the map to enlarge it._
You can find forests, typically surrounded by grassy fields, all around northern Mongolia. Generally these will be Siberian Larches, with pines and birches being common as well.
Small dirt tracks within flat, vast grassy fields are mainly found in far eastern Mongolia.
There are several areas with off-road desert coverage in southern Mongolia. Most of this coverage is directly south or east of the town of Mandalgovi.

There are a couple of paved desert roads in southern Mongolia.

_You can learn more about these roads later in the guide._
You can find arid steppe rangeland, characterised by the coarse soil, patchy grass, and small shrubs, throughout southwestern Mongolia.
These dry, rugged hills and mountains are common to see in far western Mongolia.
Lakes and rivers are much more common in western Mongolia.
Snow coverage is mostly found around Ulaanbaatar.

Fall coverage in Mongolia gives rise to very distinct orange-coloured trees and grass, and can only be found in a few areas; mostly between the towns of Lun and Hatgal, with some fall coverage around Ulaanbaatar. Trees are more commonly seen the further north you are.

NOTE: Some of the generation 4 coverage in Ulaanbaatar was also taken in the fall.

Around the town of Bugant is a large forest that stands out for having narrow dirt trails with close trees, typically on both sides, in a way that can appear quite Russian. Additionally, it is very common to see birches around this area.

Keep in mind that the dirt trails in this forest do not appear on the map.
Due to Mongolia’s harsh climate and terrain, crop fields are rare, but they do occasionally appear in the subdivisions of Selenge and Töv, near Ulaanbaatar.

The capital city, Ulaanbaatar, is by far the biggest city in Mongolia, with about 50% of the entire country's population living in it. As such, its urban development and sheer size is unlike anywhere else in Mongolia. The cityscape is bustling with many high rise buildings, chain stores, travelling cars, buses, and pedestrians, as well as clean roads and sidewalks. Meanwhile, the suburbs can be recognized from the vast yurt districts in hilly areas. Generation 4 coverage is common, however Generation 3 winter coverage is also common to see in the suburbs.

The Choir Highway is the longest covered paved road in Mongolia, running from Nalaikh down to Zamiin-Uud on the Chinese border, and is mostly desert. The dry brown soil, lack of vegetation, clear skies, and general flatness are all characteristic of this road. Additionally, a railroad runs along the entire highway, which can be seen west of the highway north of Sainshand, and east of the highway south of Sainshand. Between the towns of Sainshand and Erdene there is some overcast coverage.

The other main desert highway in Mongolia runs through Mandalgovi, and can be differentiated from the Choir Highway by its cloudy skies, darker pavement, and deep blue tent instead of the tentless car.

The Mandalgovi Highway runs south of the capital and was covered during a blizzard, making it extremely snowy and foggy. It also has a deep blue tent, which is found along this entire road, and a flat landscape which can differentiate it from other snowy roads.

The Millenium Road runs just west of the town of Lun, and has late fall coverage, combined with a dry climate that gives it characteristic orange short grass. The silver tent, clear skies, and general flatness with low rolling hills also help in identifying this road. The sun gradually sets as the car continues west until it becomes sunset at the end of the road.

NOTE: At the end of the road, the car continues travelling northwest up to Murun on off-road dirt trails.

The Darkhan-Erdenet highway can be identified by the low rolling hills, tall transmission towers, and occasional crop fields in the area. Additionally, most of the highway has winter coverage with the tentless car, light snow, and yellow grass. Beware that summer coverage can occasionally appear in the eastern half of the road.

The highway connecting the towns of Chinggis and Baruun-Urt stands out as one of the only paved highways in the east. It is considerably cloudy and the road seems freshly paved, making it a very dark road, combined with a mostly flat landscape.

A railroad can be seen along almost the entire road to the town of Khuder in the north. It is usually very close to the road, but can occasionally be quite far away, in which case it can still be identified by the mound it is built upon. In the western half of this road, the river to the south can also be seen.

Keep in mind that this railroad does not appear on the map.

While there are many unique Street View cars in Mongolia, for the sake of brevity, this guide only covers the most high-yield car metas. Car meta is very useful for Mongolia, however it is certainly possible to learn Mongolia without relying on cars.

Roads highlighted in red will only have that car, while roads highlighted in pink can have more than one car. Roads in grey are hidden coverage.

The roof racks of the Street View car are very useful as they can effectively split Mongolia in half. The presence of rubber inlays in the roof racks are generally found in the west, while empty roof racks are generally found in the east.

_You can click on the map to enlarge it._

You can split Mongolia into 4 zones based on the spare tire in the back right of the Street View car:

  • A netted spare tire shown in red
  • A single strap spare tire shown in green
  • A spare tire with no strap shown in orange
  • Without a spare tire shown in blue

_You can click on the map to enlarge it._
In the eastern grasslands, the Street View car has a light blue tent and a forward-facing snorkel.

The eastern region can be further divided into several smaller areas based on the layout of the orange roof rack straps. These straps can be seen by looking straight down.

NOTE: Orange straps can be found in the west as well, this tip is only useful for the eastern car with a blue tent from the previous tip.

_You can click on the map to enlarge it._

The tent will have red tensioner straps at the front around the city of Chinggis.

NOTE: The Chinggis-Baganuur highway (in grey) is almost entirely hidden coverage.

North of Ulaanbaatar you can find this car, which has the same blue tent as the eastern tent, but with a backwards-facing snorkel. The snorkel can sometimes be difficult to see, so use other additional clues such as rolling hills and forests to confirm the region.

NOTE: The highway in pink can have either the blue tent car or the tentless car with snow coverage.

A Street View car with no tent can be seen in and around the capital city. It is generally found on a northwest diagonal going through Ulaanbaatar. Southeast of Ulaanbaatar, on the Choir highway, the car will have a double mirror on the left as well as a backward facing snorkel.

Driving direction is especially useful with this car as it is always travelling away from the capital.

A Street View car with a bright silver tent is generally found in central and northwestern Mongolia.

NOTE: The Bulgan Highway (in grey) is almost entirely hidden coverage.
A Street View car with a grey tent and hooks on the tent can only be found in western Mongolia. It is the most common car to have the netted spare tire.
If the grey tent has hook straps angled downwards, you should be in southwestern Mongolia.
If the grey tent has no hooks on the left side and is billowing from the wind, you will be on the road between Khovd and Ölgii or around the town of Tugrug.

A Street View car with a cage on top of the roof instead of a tent can be seen near Ulaanbaatar. West of Ulaanbaatar, the car will have a green camouflage sleeping bag on top of the cage (coverage highlighted in green). Additionally, all coverage with this car was taken during winter, with most of it being in snowy areas.

NOTE: The cage car can very rarely appear in Kharkhorin and Zuunmod.

Generation 4 coverage in the capital uses a silver truck with an ornate blue & white roof decal, with a snorkel and long antenna on the front right. While the unique roof can be seen in most locations, some locations blur most of the car, leaving only the snorkel and antenna visible. This car can only be found around Ulaanbaatar.

Generation 4 coverage in eastern Mongolia uses a silver pick-up truck with a large metal box and shovel on the roof. The car was sponsored by Bodi Group, however camera stitching generally hides one of the letters.
Generation 4 coverage in western Mongolia uses a silver pick-up truck with a big light blue tent. Different variations of the tent can be useful for narrowing down the region.

The tent with 2 straps and a single knot in the straps covers most of northwestern Mongolia.

NOTE: Occasionally, camera stitching can hide the knot.
The tent with a knot on both straps covers most of southwestern Mongolia.
The tent with the lower strap in a clump covers most of central-southern Mongolia, along the road from Ulaanbaatar to Altai.
The tent with 4 straps covers most of central-northern Mongolia.
You can find a tent with an open zipper in central Mongolia, near the town of Khorgo.

Erdenet is the second largest city in Mongolia. As such, it has many multistory buildings that can be seen from across town, a large stadium, and a ferris wheel in the south of the city. It is surrounded by large barren hills to the south and to the north, and was covered on a cloudy day in the winter, meaning all vegetation is dead.

NOTE: Erdenet can look very similar to Darkhan and Ulaanbaatar, but the lack of snow distinguishes it from Darkhan, while the cloudy skies and lack of rubber inlays on the roof racks can be used to distinguish it from Ulaanbaatar.

The city of Darkhan in northern Mongolia can be recognized by its distinct snow coverage. It is the third largest city in Mongolia and as such has many high-rising buildings and travelling cars.

NOTE: Other smaller towns can also have snow coverage but Darkhan is the only large city in Mongolia with snow coverage, apart from some Ulaanbaatar suburbs.

Sukhbaatar and Altanbulag are two neighbouring towns in the north near the Russian border. They have dry, forested hills all around and heavy overcast coverage. Sukhbaatar is completely overcast while Altanbulag is slightly less cloudy.

NOTE: Murun and Choibalsan are two other towns that also have overcast coverage, but lack forested hills and have different Street View cars.

Chinggis is a major town in the east with red straps on the front of the tent. It is a fairly dry and flat town with small hills to the north, and somewhat cloudy skies.

NOTE: Dundburd and Bayan-Ovoo are the only other towns with the same tent, but are much smaller towns with no paved roads.

Choibalsan is the only major city to have several concrete roads. In most parts of the city there is a visible smoke stack, which is in the southeast corner of the city. It appears to have just rained as the roads are slightly wet and the sky is overcast. Additionally, you may occasionally find unique pedestrian signs with a short figure over three stripes.

Baruun-Urt can be identified by the towering building under construction in the centre of town (on the map its POI is called “Smile”) combined with the dry landscape.

NOTE: Similar buildings under construction can be found in other towns such as Chinggis but they are not as large and do not feature an orange tower crane like the Smile building.
The town of Khalkhgol in far east Mongolia can be recognized by its flat, green landscape with low rolling hills and a giant sword statue visible in the distance.
The town of Dariganga can be recognized by the distinctive hill present to the northwest of the town in an otherwise flat landscape.

Sainshand is the largest town in the desert region and it has a dry climate, many buildings, and paved roads. A dry ridge separates the northern and southern parts of the town, distinguishing Sainshand from other desert towns that are mostly flat. In the downtown area you can find a miniature pink eiffel tower.

The desert town of Zamiin-Uud on the border with China has unique sailboat lamp posts featuring a golden flower pot around them. Often, white signs with Mongolian folded script can be seen attached to these lamp posts.

NOTE: The other desert towns of Choir and Sainshand look similar to Zamiin-Uud and have the same Street View car but use different lamp posts. Choir can be identified by its blue lamp posts and Sainshand by its white lamp posts.

Mandalgovi is a large desert town with notably cloudy coverage. It’s the only large desert town apart from Dalanzadgad which is not on the Choir Highway, and it has a deep blue tent instead of the tentless car.

Dalanzadgad can be easily recognised by its distinct sunset coverage. Additionally it has a dry climate, fall-coloured grass, rocky hills to the south, some smoke stacks, and a unique loose tent cover on the left side.

Arvaikheer is a large central town recognizable by the warm, green, and grassy landscape in gen 4, with low rolling hills in every direction. Often you can see the town’s ferris wheel in a park in the centre of town.

NOTE: In older coverage, a distinct camera smudge can be seen on the right side of the camera.

The town of Bayankhongor, in central Mongolia, has an overall dry landscape and can be recognized from the nearby large dry hill to the east, with the Soyombo symbol inscribed onto it.

NOTE: In older coverage, a distinct camera smudge can be seen on the right side of the camera.

In the central town of Tsetserleg, you will see these distinct rocky, rugged hills, with small trees growing on them to the north. It has very clear skies and the neighbourhoods can often be seen on the hilly slopes.

Murun is a town in the north built on a north-south grid with a large jagged hill nearby to the north. It has a lot of alley coverage with dark cloudy skies and muddy, unpaved roads.

NOTE: Murun occasionally has sunny coverage where it isn’t cloudy, so consider other clues as well.

Hatgal is a small lake town on the Khuvsgul Lake. It can be recognized from its fall coverage with orange trees and grass, and the large lake in the northeast, where the Khuvsgul Ice Festival is held every year.
The small, hilly town of Tosontsengel, frequently has red-tinted roads and uses these unique lamp posts that have a wavy design.

Uliastai is a central-western Mongolian town, surrounded by large, green nearby hills. It is common to see a decent amount of trees or the river that runs through the town. In the centre of town, you can find a small hill with the Soyombo symbol inscribed on it.

In the town of Altai, you can see a range of dark, distant hills to the south and west and low rolling hills to the north and east. Additionally, it is common to see wet roads, as most of the coverage occurred after heavy rain.

NOTE: In older coverage, a unique tent can be seen, which is inflated on the left side.

Khovd is a large, dry and shrubby town, in western Mongolia, that can be identified by the very distinct rocky, red-tinted hills, present to the north of town.

NOTE: The nearby Khar-Us, Tugrug, and the samely named Khovd have similar landscapes but are much smaller towns.

Ölgii is a large town in the west, that is surrounded by close, dry rocky mountains. Towards the south end of town, there is a tall red & white radio tower, that can be seen from all across town and is quite distinct to Ölgii.

Ulaangom is a northwestern town with large, distant, dark mountains to the southwest. Additionally, these distinct double lamp posts with a blue or green painted base can frequently be seen in Ulaangom.

NOTE: Rarely, double lamp posts can be found in other cities such as Baruun-Urt and Chinggis, but these towns have flat landscapes.

In the westmost part of Mongolia, there is some very remote coverage showcasing the tallest mountains in Mongolia where you can see glaciers and snow-capped peaks. This area also has a unique Street View car with a green or black bag above the right side roof racks.

East of Uvs lake, you can find a lot of these small shrubs and patchy grass in a somewhat flat landscape.

NOTE: Similar shrubs can be found around Shaazgai Lake, but that area is considerably more hilly.

Khan Khokhii is a national park in northwestern Mongolia with some of the most dense forests in the country. It has partially cloudy skies, dark soil, and the western grey tent.

Keep in mind that the trails in this park do not appear on the map.

NOTE: There are other forests in Mongolia, but Khan Khokhii is one of the biggest and one of the only areas where you can be completely surrounded by trees.

The Gobi Gurvan Saikhan National Park, in the far south of Mongolia, features bright orange sand and sand dunes. There are two separate spots covered in the park: one in the middle just north of Sevrei, which has distant southern mountains, and the other in the far southwest corner of the park, which has a Jeep follow car.
Yolyn Am Valley is located just west of Dalanzadgad and can be identified by the extremely foggy coverage, and having dark coloured soil and hills.

This beautiful river valley, just west of Lake Hatgal in the Khoridol Saridag mountains, is very recognizable from the surrounding rocky cliffs and forests, and the ground that is completely covered in pebbles.

Mongolia has four main areas of nighttime coverage. Those areas are:

  • Northwest of Murun
  • West of Dashbalbar
  • South of Baruun-Urt
  • East of Dariganga

All of these locations are driving towards town. Driving direction and car meta can help identify which area of nighttime coverage you are in.
East of the town of Khorgo there is a large stretch of road which was driven during a rainstorm. It features much darker skies, rain drops on the camera, and occasionally a rainbow can be seen.

steps.title: Maps and resources
steps.html:
GeoGuessr’s own official maps are not very good, for a variety of reasons. Plonk It recommends you play these maps instead:

  • A Curated Mongolia - (map link) - 100k+ locs with a much more diverse and balanced distribution than the classic map. Rural locations are very common.
  • IntersectionGuessr - Mongolia - (map link) - This map contains mostly pinpointable locations in Mongolia with a high urban distribution.

In addition, here are some resources to help you practice Mongolia:

  • Plonk It Mongolia (map link) - This map contains locations for practising each meta in the Plonk It Mongolia guide from step 2 to 3.
  • Mongoliacord - (Discord link) - An invite link to the Mongolia GeoGuessr Discord.

lm.map: A Learnable Meta World - Google Cars - Basics
lm.name: Unique car
lm.note:
Gen4 Mongolia coverage was taken with two unique pickup trucks:

-White-Blue themed pickup truck mostly found only in Capital

-Pickup truck with a tent on top

lm.map: A Learnable Meta World - Google Cars - Basics
lm.name: Unique car
lm.note: The Street View car with a tent on top is unique to Mongolia. While Mongolia has other unique Google cars, this is the most common one.

lm.name: 1 knot - Northwestern
lm.note:
The tent with 2 straps and a single knot in the straps covers most of northwestern Mongolia.

NOTE: Occasionally, camera stitching can hide the knot.

Unfortunately the default single knot tent strap covers quite a large area because of this using other clues is recommended.

lm.name: 1 knot to the right - Uliastai to the Mongolian Sands
lm.note: From Uliastai to the Mongolian Sands the knot on the strap is distinctly aligned right. Getting this may require a bit of interpretation but with enough practice is easily get-able.

lm.name: 2 straps, knots left - Uliastai - Totosengel
lm.note: From just outside Uliastai to the intersection south of Telmen and around Tosontsengel you will find that the knot on the closer strap is very close to the left side of the car.

lm.name: 2 straps, knots middle - southwestern
lm.note: The tent with a knot on both straps covers most of southwestern Mongolia.

lm.name: 2 straps, no knot (perfectly packed) - Hasagt - Altai
lm.note: From the bend in the road near the place name Hasagt to the outskirts of Altai features a perfectly packed tent. This has no knots and none of the straps should be twisted(I haven’t fully checked this so feel free to contact me about it).

lm.name: 2 straps, open tent - Southeast of Totosengel
lm.note: In the stretch just after Tosontsengel you can find a variant of the open tent car. This one features only 2 straps on the car.

lm.name: 4 straps no knot - Taishir - Biger
lm.note: 4 straps with no visible knot can be found between Taishir and Biger.

lm.name: 4 straps, knot in the middle - around Tseterleg
lm.note: The tent features four straps and two knots where one of the knots is closer to the centre than the right.

lm.name: 4 straps, knot to the right - around Kharkhorin
lm.note: Mainly found around Kharkhorin is a four strap tent with both knots aligned on the right.

lm.name: 4 straps, open tent - around Khorgo
lm.note: The final section bridging the open tent and the four straps coverage is found on the road around Khorgo and features both the open tent and the four straps.

lm.name: Altai messy straps - only Altai
lm.note: A lot of the Messy Straps coverage in Altai features this strange black blur on the side of the car.

lm.name: black object - southeast of Ulaangom
lm.note: Similar to the water bottle on a section of road leading to Ulaangom there is a mysterious black object.

lm.name: messy strap, zipper left - West of Bayankhongor
lm.note: The messy strap is just a bundle of straps on the closer left strap. The messy straps are the most common being seen all the way from Altai to Ulaanbaatar. If the zipper is in the left corner of the tent(see image below) then you are west of Bayankhongor.

lm.name: messy strap, zipper right - Bayankhongor - Ulaanbaatar
lm.note: The messy strap is just a bundle of straps on the closer left strap. The messy straps are the most common being seen all the way from Altai to Ulaanbaatar. If the zipper is closer to the middle then you are east of Bayankhongor.

lm.name: open tent merged straps - between the other open tents
lm.note: On this part of the road right after the two straps you can find that the tent straps are all merged into one.

lm.name: Ulaanbaatar car - only around the capital
lm.note: Generation 4 coverage in the capital uses a silver truck with an ornate blue & white roof decal, with a snorkel and long antenna on the front right. While the unique roof can be seen in most locations, some locations blur most of the car, leaving only the snorkel and antenna visible. This car can only be found around Ulaanbaatar.

lm.name: Uliastai car - only in Uliastai
lm.note: Around the town of Uliastai you can find a very flat and empty tent. As well as the tent being visibly empty you may also see the front part of the basket which is not super common in the rest of the gen 4 coverage.

lm.name: water bottle - Hüryee - Songino
lm.note: From the edge of Khyargas lake to Songino a plastic water bottle can be seen hanging out of the google car.

lm.note: Snow coverage is mostly found around Ulaanbaatar.

lm.name: Gen3Car  -  "Cage Car"
lm.note: A Street View car with a cage on top of the roof instead of a tent can be seen near Ulaanbaatar. West of Ulaanbaatar, the car will have a green camouflage sleeping bag on top of the cage (coverage highlighted in green). Additionally, all coverage with this car was taken during winter, with most of it being in snowy areas.

lm.name: Gen3Car  -  Choir HW Double Mirror
lm.note: The Choir Highway features an unique Gen 3 Car without a tent but with a double mirror on its left side

lm.name: Gen3Car  -  Lightblue Tent Snorkel Backwards
lm.note:
North of Ulaanbaatar you can find this car, which has the same blue tent as the eastern tent, but with a backwards-facing snorkel. The snorkel can sometimes be difficult to see, so use other additional clues such as rolling hills and forests to confirm the region.

NOTE: The highway in pink can have either the blue tent car or the tentless car with snow coverage.

lm.name: Gen3Car  - Bright Silver Tent
lm.note:
A Street View car with a bright silver tent is generally found in central and northwestern Mongolia.

NOTE: The Bulgan Highway (in grey) is almost entirely hidden coverage.

lm.name: Gen3Car  - Chinggis Red Tensioners
lm.note:
The tent will have red tensioner straps at the front around the city of Chinggis.

NOTE: The Chinggis-Baganuur highway (in grey) is almost entirely hidden coverage.

lm.name: Gen3Car  - Deep Blue Tent
lm.note: A Car with a deep blue tent w/o hooks is found on and around the Mandalgovi Highway.

lm.name: Gen3Car  - Grey Tent w/ Hooks
lm.note: A Street View car with a grey tent and hooks on the tent can only be found in western Mongolia. It is the most common car to have the netted spare tire.

lm.name: Gen3Car  - Grey Tent w/ Hooks, Strips angled downwards
lm.note: If the grey tent has hook straps angled downwards, you should be in southwestern Mongolia.

lm.name: Gen3Car  - Khovd Windy HW
lm.note: the grey tent has no hooks on the left side and is billowing from the wind, you will be on the road between Khovd and Ölgii or around the town of Tugrug.

lm.name: Gen3Car  - Lightblue Tent Snorkel Forward
lm.note: In the eastern grasslands, the Street View car has a light blue tent and a forward-facing snorkel.

lm.name: Gen3Car  - No Tent
lm.note:
A Street View car with no tent can be seen in and around the capital city. It is generally found on a northwest diagonal going through Ulaanbaatar. Southeast of Ulaanbaatar, on the Choir highway, the car will have a double mirror on the left as well as a backward facing snorkel.

Driving direction is especially useful with this car as it is always travelling away from the capital.

lm.name: Gen3Car  - Windy Tent Dalanzadgad Highway
lm.note: Similar to the Khovd Highway the road west of Dalanzadgad and the town itself has a broken tent on top of the google car.

lm.name: Gen3Tire  - Netted Spare Tire
lm.note:
You can split Mongolia into 4 zones based on the spare tire in the back right of the Street View car:

A netted spare tire shown in red

A single strap spare tire shown in green

A spare tire with no strap shown in orange

Without a spare tire shown in blue

lm.name: Gen3Tire  - No Strip on the spare tire
lm.note:
You can split Mongolia into 4 zones based on the spare tire in the back right of the Street View car:

A netted spare tire shown in red

A single strap spare tire shown in green

A spare tire with no strap shown in orange

Without a spare tire shown in blue

lm.name: Gen3Tire  - Single Stripe on spare tire
lm.note:
You can split Mongolia into 4 zones based on the spare tire in the back right of the Street View car:

A netted spare tire shown in red

A single strap spare tire shown in green

A spare tire with no strap shown in orange

Without a spare tire shown in blue

lm.name: Gen4  - Coverage
lm.note: Recently released Generation 4 coverage in Mongolia currently can only be found in Ulaanbaatar and throughout western Mongolia.

lm.name: Gen4Car  -  2Straps 1Knob
lm.note:
The tent with 2 straps and a single knot in the straps covers most of northwestern Mongolia.

NOTE: Occasionally, camera stitching can hide the knot.

lm.name: Gen4Car  -  East Tosontsengel Open Tent
lm.note: You can find a tent with an open zipper in central Mongolia, near the town of Khorgo.

lm.name: Gen4Car  -  Lower Strap in Clump
lm.note: The tent with the lower strap in a clump covers most of central-southern Mongolia, along the road from Ulaanbaatar to Altai.

lm.name: Gen4Car  - 2Straps 2Knobs
lm.note: The tent with a knot on both straps covers most of southwestern Mongolia.

lm.name: Gen4Car  - 4 Straps
lm.note: The tent with 4 straps covers most of central-northern Mongolia.

lm.name: Gen4Car  - Ulaanbaatar Area
lm.note: Generation 4 coverage in the capital uses a silver truck with an ornate blue & white roof decal, with a snorkel and long antenna on the front right. While the unique roof can be seen in most locations, some locations blur most of the car, leaving only the snorkel and antenna visible. This car can only be found around Ulaanbaatar.

lm.name: Khovd  - City
lm.note:
Khovd is a large, dry and shrubby town, in western Mongolia, that can be identified by the very distinct rocky, red-tinted hills, present to the north of town. It also has the windy tent coverage in Gen 3.

NOTE: The nearby Khar-Us, Tugrug, and the samely named Khovd have similar landscapes but are much smaller towns.

lm.name: Landscape  - Bugant Forrests
lm.note:
Around the town of Bugant is a large forest that stands out for having narrow dirt trails with close trees, typically on both sides, in a way that can appear quite Russian. Additionally, it is very common to see birches around this area.

Keep in mind that the dirt trails in this forest do not appear on the map.

lm.name: Landscape  - Desert
lm.note: On the two main highways that run south of the capital is a desert landscape.

lm.name: Landscape  - Flat Green East
lm.note: Small dirt tracks within flat, vast grassy fields are mainly found in far eastern Mongolia.

lm.name: Landscape  - Khan Khokhii Forrest
lm.note:
Khan Khokhii is a national park in northwestern Mongolia with some of the most dense forests in the country. It has partially cloudy skies, dark soil, and the western grey tent.

Keep in mind that the trails in this park do not appear on the map.

NOTE: There are other forests in Mongolia, but Khan Khokhii is one of the biggest and one of the only areas where you can be completely surrounded by trees.

lm.name: Landscape  - Khyargas Lake
lm.note: The largest covered lake in Mongolia. The lake will always be S/SE with a desertish landscape and big hills behind the lake

lm.name: Landscape  - Tolbo Lake
lm.note: Tolbo Lake is one of two large lakes with coverage right next to it. It is hillyand quite green with the lake to your S/SE

lm.name: Landscape  - Western Mountains
lm.note: In the westmost part of Mongolia, there is some very remote coverage showcasing the tallest mountains in Mongolia where you can see glaciers and snow-capped peaks. This area also has a unique Street View car with a green or black bag above the right side roof racks.

lm.name: Mandalgovi  - Unique Highway
lm.note: The other main desert highway in Mongolia runs through Mandalgovi, and can be differentiated from the Choir Highway by its cloudy skies, darker pavement, and deep blue tent instead of the tentless car. North of Mandalgovi there is extreme snowcoverage due to a blizzard

lm.name: Trekker  - Dariganga Hill
lm.note: Right outside of Dariganga there is a Trekker walking on a hill. You'll always either see the town in SE direction or a distinct building on top of the hill.

lm.name: Tsetserleg  - Unique City
lm.note: In the central town of Tsetserleg, you will see these distinct rocky, rugged hills, with small trees growing on them to the north. It has very clear skies and the neighbourhoods can often be seen on the hilly slopes. Note: It also has Gen 3 bright silver tent coverage

lm.name: Ulaanbaatar  - Capital City
lm.note: The capital city, Ulaanbaatar, is by far the biggest city in Mongolia, with about 50% of the entire country's population living in it. As such, its urban development and sheer size is unlike anywhere else in Mongolia. The cityscape is bustling with many high rise buildings, chain stores, travelling cars, buses, and pedestrians, as well as clean roads and sidewalks. Meanwhile, the suburbs can be recognized from the vast yurt districts in hilly areas. Generation 4 coverage is common, however Generation 3 winter coverage is also common to see in the suburbs.

lm.name: Zamiin - City
lm.note:
The desert town of Zamiin-Uud on the border with China has unique sailboat lamp posts featuring a golden flower pot around them. Often, white signs with Mongolian folded script can be seen attached to these lamp posts. Also you will often see lots of traffic and trucks due to its border with China.

NOTE: The other desert towns of Choir and Sainshand look similar to Zamiin-Uud and have the same Street View car but use different lamp posts. Choir can be identified by its blue lamp posts and Sainshand by its white lamp posts.

lm.name: Altai car
lm.note: North and south of Altai, the Google car in Gen 4 has its tent tied down with four neatly packed straps. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

lm.name: Black object
lm.note: On a short stretch of the road leading to Ulaangrom in the Northwest of the country, east of Tarialan, there is a black object visible on the left side of the truck bed. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

lm.name: Four straps open tent
lm.note: The zipper of tent on the Google car is open on a stretch of road between Tosontsengel and the Teel area. When there are four straps visible, you will be on the eastern part of that coverage. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

lm.name: Into the night
lm.note: On a road in northeastern Mongolia, the Google car drove through sunset into nighttime. There is a second road in the southeast with sunset coverage, which can be distinguished by the driving angle: this one goes east, the one in the South goes north.

lm.name: Into the night, part 2
lm.note: In southeastern Mongolia, the Google car drove until after sunset. You can see the shadows becoming longer and the footage eventually turns very dark. This can be told apart from the other sunset road in the northeast by the driving angle - this one goes north, the other one goes east.

lm.name: Messy straps no loop
lm.note: From Bayankhongor to Arvaikheer, Gen 4 coverage will have two straps with a messy knot. The mess is one clump with no loose loops. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

lm.name: Messy straps with loop
lm.note: From Arvaikheer to Ulaanbaatar, Gen 4 coverage will have two straps with a messy knot that has a loose loop. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

lm.name: Messy straps zipper corner
lm.note: Between Altai and Bayankhongor, Gen 4 coverage will have two straps with a messy knot. While further east, the zipper tag is a bit more central, on this part of the road it is all the way left. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

lm.name: Open tent merged straps
lm.note: The zipper of tent on the Google car is open on a stretch of road between Tosontsengel and the Teel area. When there are four straps converging into a single point on the left side, you will be on a north-south bit in the middle of that coverage. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

lm.name: Open tent two straps
lm.note: The zipper of tent on the Google car is open on a stretch of road between Tosontsengel and the Teel area. When there are just two straps visible, you will be on the westernmost part of that coverage. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

lm.name: Perfectly packed
lm.note: West of Altai until about Sharga, the Google car in Gen 4 has its tent tied down with two neatly packed straps, no knots. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

lm.name: Single knot right (2 straps)
lm.note: In the West and Northwest of the country, the tent on the car in Gen4 coverage is usually tied with two straps and a single knot visible in the center of the tent or to the left. When the knot is slightly on the right of the tent, you will be on one specific road between Durvuljin and Uliastai. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

lm.name: Two knots left (2 straps)
lm.note: In the Southwest of the country, the tent on the car in Gen4 coverage is usually tied with two straps and two knots on the right side. If the knots are on the left instead, you will be on one of two specific stretches of road around the Tarvagatai Mountains. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

lm.name: Two knots right (4 straps)
lm.note: Between Khotont and Lun, you will find four straps tying down the tent on the Google car in Gen4, with both knots on the right side. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

lm.name: Two knots, one center (4 straps)
lm.note: Around Tsetserleg, you will find four straps tying down the tent on the Google car in Gen4, with one of the two knots in the center of the tent and the other one on the right side. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

lm.name: Water bottle
lm.note: Between Khyargas Lake and Songino, a water bottle will be visible on the left side of the truck bed. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

lm.name: Filled Crossbar
lm.note: The slot in the middle of the crossbar is filled in with black cover strips in the western half of the country. The slot is empty in the eastern half.

lm.name: Tentless Car
lm.note: The tentless car’s coverage is all near the midline of the capital (Ulaanbaatar). This car will never be found far east or west.

lm.name: Unfilled Crossbar
lm.note: The slot in the middle of the crossbar is filled in with black cover strips in the western half of the country. The slot is empty in the eastern half.

lm.name: 4 Straps
lm.note: The tent with 4 straps covers most of central-northern Mongolia.

lm.name: Altai
lm.note:
In the town of Altai, you can see a range of dark, distant hills to the south and west and low rolling hills to the north and east. Additionally, it is common to see wet roads, as most of the coverage occurred after heavy rain.

NOTE: In older coverage, a unique tent can be seen, which is inflated on the left side.

lm.name: Arid Steppe Rangeland
lm.note: You can find arid steppe rangeland, characterised by the coarse soil, patchy grass, and small shrubs, throughout southwestern Mongolia.

lm.name: Arvaikheer
lm.note:
Arvaikheer is a large central town recognizable by the warm, green, and grassy landscape in gen 4, with low rolling hills in every direction. Often you can see the town’s ferris wheel in a park in the centre of town.

NOTE: In older coverage, a distinct camera smudge can be seen on the right side of the camera.

lm.name: Backwards-Facing Snorkel
lm.note:
North of Ulaanbaatar you can find this car, which has the same blue tent as the eastern tent, but with a backwards-facing snorkel. The snorkel can sometimes be difficult to see, so use other additional clues such as rolling hills and forests to confirm the region.

NOTE: The highway in pink can have either the blue tent car or the tentless car with snow coverage.

lm.name: Baruun-Urt
lm.note:
Baruun-Urt can be identified by the towering building under construction in the centre of town (on the map its POI is called “Smile”) combined with the dry landscape.

NOTE: Similar buildings under construction can be found in other towns such as Chinggis but they are not as large and do not feature an orange tower crane like the Smile building.

lm.name: Bayankhongor
lm.note:
The town of Bayankhongor, in central Mongolia, has an overall dry landscape and can be recognized from the nearby large dry hill to the east, with the Soyombo symbol inscribed onto it.

NOTE: In older coverage, a distinct camera smudge can be seen on the right side of the camera.

lm.name: Car With Cage
lm.note:
A Street View car with a cage on top of the roof instead of a tent can be seen near Ulaanbaatar. West of Ulaanbaatar, the car will have a green camouflage sleeping bag on top of the cage (coverage highlighted in green). Additionally, all coverage with this car was taken during winter, with most of it being in snowy areas.

NOTE: The cage car can very rarely appear in Kharkhorin and Zuunmod.

lm.name: Chinggis
lm.note:
Chinggis is a major town in the east with red straps on the front of the tent. It is a fairly dry and flat town with small hills to the north, and somewhat cloudy skies.

NOTE: Dundburd and Bayan-Ovoo are the only other towns with the same tent, but are much smaller towns with no paved roads.

lm.name: Choibalsan
lm.note: Choibalsan is the only major city to have several concrete roads. In most parts of the city there is a visible smoke stack, which is in the southeast corner of the city. It appears to have just rained as the roads are slightly wet and the sky is overcast. Additionally, you may occasionally find unique pedestrian signs with a short figure over three stripes.

lm.name: Choir Highway
lm.note: The Choir Highway is the longest covered paved road in Mongolia, running from Nalaikh down to Zamiin-Uud on the Chinese border, and is mostly desert. The dry brown soil, lack of vegetation, clear skies, and general flatness are all characteristic of this road. Additionally, a railroad runs along the entire highway, which can be seen west of the highway north of Sainshand, and east of the highway south of Sainshand. Between the towns of Sainshand and Erdene there is some overcast coverage.

lm.name: Crop Fields
lm.note: Due to Mongolia’s harsh climate and terrain, crop fields are rare, but they do occasionally appear in the subdivisions of Selenge and Töv, near Ulaanbaatar.

lm.name: Dalanzadgad
lm.note: Dalanzadgad can be easily recognised by its distinct sunset coverage. Additionally it has a dry climate, fall-coloured grass, rocky hills to the south, some smoke stacks, and a unique loose tent cover on the left side.

lm.name: Dariganga
lm.note: The town of Dariganga can be recognized by the distinctive hill present to the northwest of the town in an otherwise flat landscape.

lm.name: Darkhan
lm.note:
The city of Darkhan in northern Mongolia can be recognized by its distinct snow coverage. It is the third largest city in Mongolia and as such has many high-rising buildings and travelling cars.

NOTE: Other smaller towns can also have snow coverage but Darkhan is the only large city in Mongolia with snow coverage, apart from some Ulaanbaatar suburbs.

lm.name: Darkhan-Erdenet Hwy.
lm.note: The Darkhan-Erdenet highway can be identified by the low rolling hills, tall transmission towers, and occasional crop fields in the area. Additionally, most of the highway has winter coverage with the tentless car, light snow, and yellow grass. Beware that summer coverage can occasionally appear in the eastern half of the road.

lm.name: Dense Forest
lm.note:
Khan Khokhii is a national park in northwestern Mongolia with some of the most dense forests in the country. It has partially cloudy skies, dark soil, and the western grey tent.

Keep in mind that the trails in this park do not appear on the map.

NOTE: There are other forests in Mongolia, but Khan Khokhii is one of the biggest and one of the only areas where you can be completely surrounded by trees.

lm.name: Dry, Rugged Hills and Mountains
lm.note: These dry, rugged hills and mountains are common to see in far western Mongolia.

lm.name: Eastern Grassland Car
lm.note: In the eastern grasslands, the Street View car has a light blue tent and a forward-facing snorkel.

lm.name: Empty Roof Racks
lm.note: The roof racks of the Street View car are very useful as they can effectively split Mongolia in half. The presence of rubber inlays in the roof racks are generally found in the west, while empty roof racks are generally found in the east.

lm.name: Erdenet
lm.note:
Erdenet is the second largest city in Mongolia. As such, it has many multistory buildings that can be seen from across town, a large stadium, and a ferris wheel in the south of the city. It is surrounded by large barren hills to the south and to the north, and was covered on a cloudy day in the winter, meaning all vegetation is dead.

NOTE: Erdenet can look very similar to Darkhan and Ulaanbaatar, but the lack of snow distinguishes it from Darkhan, while the cloudy skies and lack of rubber inlays on the roof racks can be used to distinguish it from Ulaanbaatar.

lm.name: Extremly Snowy Coverage
lm.note: The Mandalgovi Highway runs south of the capital and was covered during a blizzard, making it extremely snowy and foggy. It also has a deep blue tent, which is found along this entire road, and a flat landscape which can differentiate it from other snowy roads.

lm.name: Fall Coverage
lm.note:
Fall coverage in Mongolia gives rise to very distinct orange-coloured trees and grass, and can only be found in a few areas; mostly between the towns of Lun and Hatgal, with some fall coverage around Ulaanbaatar. Trees are more commonly seen the further north you are.

NOTE: Some of the generation 4 coverage in Ulaanbaatar was also taken in the fall.

lm.name: Forests
lm.note: You can find forests, typically surrounded by grassy fields, all around northern Mongolia. Generally these will be Siberian Larches, with pines and birches being common as well.

lm.name: Gobi Gurvan Saikhan National Park
lm.note: The Gobi Gurvan Saikhan National Park, in the far south of Mongolia, features bright orange sand and sand dunes. There are two separate spots covered in the park: one in the middle just north of Sevrei, which has distant southern mountains, and the other in the far southwest corner of the park, which has a Jeep follow car.

lm.name: Grey Tent Car
lm.note: A Street View car with a grey tent and hooks on the tent can only be found in western Mongolia. It is the most common car to have the netted spare tire.

lm.name: Hatgal
lm.note: Hatgal is a small lake town on the Khuvsgul Lake. It can be recognized from its fall coverage with orange trees and grass, and the large lake in the northeast, where the Khuvsgul Ice Festival is held every year.

lm.name: Hook Straps Car
lm.note: If the grey tent has hook straps angled downwards, you should be in southwestern Mongolia.

lm.name: Khalkhgol
lm.note: The town of Khalkhgol in far east Mongolia can be recognized by its flat, green landscape with low rolling hills and a giant sword statue visible in the distance.

lm.name: Khovd
lm.note:
Khovd is a large, dry and shrubby town, in western Mongolia, that can be identified by the very distinct rocky, red-tinted hills, present to the north of town.

NOTE: The nearby Khar-Us, Tugrug, and the samely named Khovd have similar landscapes but are much smaller towns.

lm.name: Knot on Both Straps
lm.note: The tent with a knot on both straps covers most of southwestern Mongolia.

lm.name: Lakes/Rivers
lm.note: Lakes and rivers are much more common in western Mongolia.

lm.name: Mandalgovi
lm.note: Mandalgovi is a large desert town with notably cloudy coverage. It’s the only large desert town apart from Dalanzadgad which is not on the Choir Highway, and it has a deep blue tent instead of the tentless car.

lm.name: Mandalgovi Rd.
lm.note: The other main desert highway in Mongolia runs through Mandalgovi, and can be differentiated from the Choir Highway by its cloudy skies, darker pavement, and deep blue tent instead of the tentless car.

lm.name: Murun
lm.note:
Murun is a town in the north built on a north-south grid with a large jagged hill nearby to the north. It has a lot of alley coverage with dark cloudy skies and muddy, unpaved roads.

NOTE: Murun occasionally has sunny coverage where it isn’t cloudy, so consider other clues as well.

lm.name: Narrow Dirt Trails
lm.note:
Around the town of Bugant is a large forest that stands out for having narrow dirt trails with close trees, typically on both sides, in a way that can appear quite Russian. Additionally, it is very common to see birches around this area.

Keep in mind that the dirt trails in this forest do not appear on the map.

lm.name: Netted Spare Tire
lm.note:
You can split Mongolia into 4 zones based on the spare tire in the back right of the Street View car:

A netted spare tire shown in red

lm.name: Night Coverage
lm.note:
Mongolia has four main areas of nighttime coverage. Those areas are:

  • Northwest of Murun
  • West of Dashbalbar
  • South of Baruun-Urt
  • East of Dariganga

All of these locations are driving towards town. Driving direction and car meta can help identify which area of nighttime coverage you are in.

lm.name: No Hooks Car
lm.note: If the grey tent has no hooks on the left side and is billowing from the wind, you will be on the road between Khovd and Ölgii or around the town of Tugrug.

lm.name: No Spare Tire
lm.note:
You can split Mongolia into 4 zones based on the spare tire in the back right of the Street View car:

Without a spare tire shown in blue

lm.name: No Tent Car
lm.note:
A Street View car with no tent can be seen in and around the capital city. It is generally found on a northwest diagonal going through Ulaanbaatar. Southeast of Ulaanbaatar, on the Choir highway, the car will have a double mirror on the left as well as a backward facing snorkel.

Driving direction is especially useful with this car as it is always travelling away from the capital.

lm.name: Off-Road Desert Coverage
lm.note: There are several areas with off-road desert coverage in southern Mongolia. Most of this coverage is directly south or east of the town of Mandalgovi.

lm.name: Ölgii
lm.note: Ölgii is a large town in the west, that is surrounded by close, dry rocky mountains. Towards the south end of town, there is a tall red & white radio tower, that can be seen from all across town and is quite distinct to Ölgii.

lm.name: Open Zipper
lm.note: You can find a tent with an open zipper in central Mongolia, near the town of Khorgo.

lm.name: Orange Short Grass
lm.note:
The Millenium Road runs just west of the town of Lun, and has late fall coverage, combined with a dry climate that gives it characteristic orange short grass. The silver tent, clear skies, and general flatness with low rolling hills also help in identifying this road. The sun gradually sets as the car continues west until it becomes sunset at the end of the road.

NOTE: At the end of the road, the car continues travelling northwest up to Murun on off-road dirt trails.

lm.name: Paved Desert Road
lm.note: There are a couple of paved desert roads in southern Mongolia.

lm.name: Red Tensioner Strap
lm.note:
The tent will have red tensioner straps at the front around the city of Chinggis.

NOTE: The Chinggis-Baganuur highway (in grey) is almost entirely hidden coverage.

lm.name: River Valley
lm.note: This beautiful river valley, just west of Lake Hatgal in the Khoridol Saridag mountains, is very recognizable from the surrounding rocky cliffs and forests, and the ground that is completely covered in pebbles.

lm.name: Roof Decal Car
lm.note: Generation 4 coverage in the capital uses a silver truck with an ornate blue & white roof decal, with a snorkel and long antenna on the front right. While the unique roof can be seen in most locations, some locations blur most of the car, leaving only the snorkel and antenna visible. This car can only be found around Ulaanbaatar.

lm.name: Roof Racks With Rubber
lm.note: The roof racks of the Street View car are very useful as they can effectively split Mongolia in half. The presence of rubber inlays in the roof racks are generally found in the west, while empty roof racks are generally found in the east.

lm.name: Sainshand
lm.note: Sainshand is the largest town in the desert region and it has a dry climate, many buildings, and paved roads. A dry ridge separates the northern and southern parts of the town, distinguishing Sainshand from other desert towns that are mostly flat. In the downtown area you can find a miniature pink eiffel tower.

lm.name: Silver Car
lm.note: Generation 4 coverage in western Mongolia uses a silver pick-up truck with a big light blue tent. Different variations of the tent can be useful for narrowing down the region.

lm.name: Silver Tent Car
lm.note:
A Street View car with a bright silver tent is generally found in central and northwestern Mongolia.

NOTE: The Bulgan Highway (in grey) is almost entirely hidden coverage.

lm.name: Single Knot Car
lm.note:
The tent with 2 straps and a single knot in the straps covers most of northwestern Mongolia.

NOTE: Occasionally, camera stitching can hide the knot.

lm.name: Single Strap Spare Tire
lm.note:
You can split Mongolia into 4 zones based on the spare tire in the back right of the Street View car:

A single strap spare tire shown in green

lm.name: Small Shrubs
lm.note:
East of Uvs lake, you can find a lot of these small shrubs and patchy grass in a somewhat flat landscape.

NOTE: Similar shrubs can be found around Shaazgai Lake, but that area is considerably more hilly.

lm.name: Snow Coverage
lm.note: Snow coverage is mostly found around Ulaanbaatar.

lm.name: Snow-Capped Peaks
lm.note: In the westmost part of Mongolia, there is some very remote coverage showcasing the tallest mountains in Mongolia where you can see glaciers and snow-capped peaks. This area also has a unique Street View car with a green or black bag above the right side roof racks.

lm.name: Spare Tire With No Strap
lm.note:
You can split Mongolia into 4 zones based on the spare tire in the back right of the Street View car:

A spare tire with no strap shown in orange

lm.name: Strap In Clump
lm.note: The tent with the lower strap in a clump covers most of central-southern Mongolia, along the road from Ulaanbaatar to Altai.

lm.name: Straps-Layout
lm.note:
The eastern region can be further divided into several smaller areas based on the layout of the orange roof rack straps. These straps can be seen by looking straight down.

NOTE: Orange straps can be found in the west as well, this tip is only useful for the eastern car with a blue tent from the previous tip.

lm.name: Sükhbaatar/Altanbulag
lm.note:
Sükhbaatar and Altanbulag are two neighbouring towns in the north near the Russian border. They have dry, forested hills all around and heavy overcast coverage. Sukhbaatar is completely overcast while Altanbulag is slightly less cloudy.

NOTE: Murun and Choibalsan are two other towns that also have overcast coverage, but lack forested hills and have different Street View cars.

lm.name: Tosontsengel
lm.note: The small, hilly town of Tosontsengel, frequently has red-tinted roads and uses these unique lamp posts that have a wavy design.

lm.name: Tsetserleg
lm.note: In the central town of Tsetserleg, you will see these distinct rocky, rugged hills, with small trees growing on them to the north. It has very clear skies and the neighbourhoods can often be seen on the hilly slopes.

lm.name: Ulaanbaatar
lm.note: The capital city, Ulaanbaatar, is by far the biggest city in Mongolia, with about 50% of the entire country's population living in it. As such, its urban development and sheer size is unlike anywhere else in Mongolia. The cityscape is bustling with many high rise buildings, chain stores, travelling cars, buses, and pedestrians, as well as clean roads and sidewalks. Meanwhile, the suburbs can be recognized from the vast yurt districts in hilly areas. Generation 4 coverage is common, however Generation 3 winter coverage is also common to see in the suburbs.

lm.name: Ulaangom
lm.note:
Ulaangom is a northwestern town with large, distant, dark mountains to the southwest. Additionally, these distinct double lamp posts with a blue or green painted base can frequently be seen in Ulaangom.

NOTE: Rarely, double lamp posts can be found in other cities such as Baruun-Urt and Chinggis, but these towns have flat landscapes.

lm.name: Uliastai
lm.note: Uliastai is a central-western Mongolian town, surrounded by large, green nearby hills. It is common to see a decent amount of trees or the river that runs through the town. In the centre of town, you can find a small hill with the Soyombo symbol inscribed on it.

lm.name: Vast Grassy Fields
lm.note: Small dirt tracks within flat, vast grassy fields are mainly found in far eastern Mongolia.

lm.name: Yolyn Am Valley
lm.note: Yolyn Am Valley is located just west of Dalanzadgad and can be identified by the extremely foggy coverage, and having dark coloured soil and hills.

lm.name: Zamiin-Uud
lm.note:
The desert town of Zamiin-Uud on the border with China has unique sailboat lamp posts featuring a golden flower pot around them. Often, white signs with Mongolian folded script can be seen attached to these lamp posts.

NOTE: The other desert towns of Choir and Sainshand look similar to Zamiin-Uud and have the same Street View car but use different lamp posts. Choir can be identified by its blue lamp posts and Sainshand by its white lamp posts.

top.html: Mongolian licence plates are mostly white with a hint of red on the left side from the Soyombo symbol.
top.raw: Mongolian licence plates are mostly white with a hint of **red** on the left side from the [Soyombo symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyombo_symbol).

top.html:
Mongolia primarily uses Cyrillic script, though Latin and traditional Mongolian script can also occasionally be seen. Mongolian Cyrillic contains the letters Ɵ and Ү, which do not exist in the Russian alphabet. Additionally, the use of double vowels, such as aa, ƟƟ or ЭЭ, is common in Mongolian.

NOTE: The letters Ɵ and Ү also exist in the Kyrgyz and Kazakh languages.
top.raw: Mongolia primarily uses **Cyrillic **script, though [Latin](https://www.google.com/maps/@47.912178,106.980081,3a,17.5y,297.7h,98.09t/data=!3m4!1e1!3m2!1s5Bf-6kOlFPU1X7Sd37ewaw!2e0) and [traditional Mongolian](https://www.google.com/maps/@49.0335237,111.6546939,2a,63.5y,344.76h,97.65t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1s3xuVpyvGy0UEgWOxX2rmTA!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu) script can also occasionally be seen. Mongolian Cyrillic contains the letters **Ɵ** and **Ү**,** **which do not exist in the Russian alphabet. Additionally, the use of **double vowels**,** **such as aa, ƟƟ or ЭЭ, is common in Mongolian. NOTE: The letters **Ɵ** and **Ү **also exist in the Kyrgyz and Kazakh languages.

top.html: Mongolia very often has a visible Street View car as all of Mongolian coverage was driven with a large pickup truck. The truck can have several features such as a tent on top, red side-view mirrors, a snorkel, and roof-racks. All of these can be of help in identifying Mongolia.
top.raw: Mongolia very often has a visible Street View car as all of Mongolian coverage was driven with a large pickup truck. The truck can have several features such as a **tent **on top, **red** **side-view mirrors**, a **snorkel,** and **roof-racks.** All of these can be of help in identifying Mongolia.

top.html: Mongolia can typically be identified by the steppe biomes found across the country. While some forested areas are found in Mongolia, most of the country features empty grasslands or deserts with a characteristic lack of trees. It is not uncommon to find rugged, rocky or rolling hills as well as rivers and lakes across Mongolia.
top.raw: Mongolia can typically be identified by the **steppe biomes** found across the country. While some forested areas are found in Mongolia, most of the country features empty grasslands or deserts with a characteristic **lack of trees**. It is not uncommon to find rugged, rocky or rolling hills as well as rivers and lakes across Mongolia.

top.html: Mongolia uniquely features white bowling-pin shaped bollards with two red stripes around the top.
top.raw: Mongolia uniquely features white **bowling-pin shaped bollards** with two red stripes around the top.

top.html:
Mongolian infrastructure has clear Russian influence. Wooden poles with supporting stone blocks, white lamp posts, and three-striped pedestrian crossing signs are common to see.

Unique to Mongolia is the “ЗОГС” stop sign.

NOTE: Each town has unique lamp post designs, so learning them can be quite useful.
top.raw: Mongolian infrastructure has clear Russian influence. Wooden poles with supporting stone blocks, [white lamp posts](https://www.google.com/maps/@46.677839,113.270184,3a,64.1y,330.3h,92.79t/data=!3m4!1e1!3m2!1sAv0lfNtDl5QLj3rxCnkYzA!2e0), and [three-striped** **pedestrian crossing signs](https://www.google.com/maps/@50.2393538,106.2025013,2a,60y,95.51h,75.52t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sXUNd4wtT71dkoiStvdsI-Q!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu) are common to see. Unique to Mongolia is the** **[**“ЗОГС”**](https://www.google.com/maps/@50.2286946,106.2131419,2a,15y,73.91h,86.02t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sDbSJ2KjqHFeQw_Vx-Muhyg!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu)** stop sign**. NOTE: Each town has unique lamp post designs, so learning them can be quite useful.

top.html: Mongolian neighbourhoods are very frequently separated by dirt alleys and wooden fences.
top.raw: Mongolian neighbourhoods are very frequently separated by **dirt alleys **and wooden fences.

top.html: White, round yurts are the traditional dwelling of nomadic families in Mongolia, and are often seen all around the country.
top.raw: White, round **yurts** are the traditional dwelling of nomadic families in Mongolia, and are often seen all around the country.

top.html: It is very common to see large herds of animals in Mongolia, including horses, yaks, cows, sheep, goats, and camels.
top.raw: It is very common to see** **large **herds of animals** in Mongolia, including horses, yaks, cows, sheep, goats, and camels.

top.html: Decorated piles of stones, known as ovoos, are used as ceremonial markers or shrines throughout Mongolia and are common to see.
top.raw: Decorated piles of stones, known as **[ovoos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovoo)**, are used as ceremonial markers or shrines throughout Mongolia and are common to see.
